remaining_partial_contracts: Native Move and move construction leave the source as a non-owning alias with unchanged pointer/range. Safe Rust move_from empties the source. The oracle records native-source-alias separately; this difference is not approved as parity.
Only the default 16-byte native alignment policy is represented; MyAlignSize template policies remain unported.
Native const external pointers may be written through a cast; safe Rust only accepts an exclusive mutable slice, and signed prefix construction checks that the slice is long enough.
Typed APIs accept ArrayValue/Pod types only; arbitrary C++ object representations, assignment hooks, overlapping writable aliases, and unaligned reference access are not claimed.

Rust fresh allocation zeroes bytes and checks byte-count overflow; native fresh bytes are indeterminate and native stride narrowing can truncate a size_t larger than UINT32_MAX. Existing Rust checked_stride rejects those strides.

Allocator hook policy and out-of-memory behavior are not equivalent. Native discard-resize frees owned storage before allocation; existing Rust resize allocates replacement storage before dropping the old block.
No new integrated API or original declaration mapping credit; candidate bindings need compiler-backed symbol capture and final integration validation.
